sentences.text: Piatnitzkysaurus was a medium-sized theropod dinosaur with a light frame and strong forelimbs, reaching lengths between four and five meters and weighing up to 275 kilograms.
Scientists estimate that fully grown adults of this species could have stretched to 6.6 meters in total length.
The skull measured 50 centimeters long and contained large openings that helped reduce its overall weight.
Its mouth held conical, highly compressed teeth that curved backward and ended in sharp points.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, represented a subadult individual estimated to be around 4.3 meters long and 450 kilograms in mass.
Piatnitzkysaurus is the only member of its family with preserved cranial material, including two maxillae, a frontal bone, a skull, and a partial dentary.
This dinosaur is remarkable for having robust arms despite its light build and medium size.
The holotype specimen was collected during expeditions in 1977, 1982, and 1983 from the Cañadón Asfalto Formation.
The type species Piatnitzkysaurus floresi was described by Jose Bonaparte in 1979.
The genus name Piatnitzkysaurus was named to honor Alejandro Matveievich Piatnitzky, a Russian-born Argentine geologist.
Its light build would have conferred great speed on Piatnitzkysaurus.
When holding its prey with its jaws, Piatnitzkysaurus's claws would wound the flesh, causing bleeding until the prey was too weak to resist.
Piatnitzkysaurus is classified in the family Piatnitzkysauridae.
Piatnitzkysaurus floresi is the only known species in the genus Piatnitzkysaurus, a megalosauroid theropod dinosaur.
Piatnitzkysaurus is part of the most basal clade within Megalosauroidea, which also contains Condorraptor, Marshosaurus, and Xuanhanosaurus.
It is debated whether Condorraptor is a distinct species or merely individual variation within Piatnitzkysaurus due to their strong resemblance.
It is debated whether the affiliation of Piatnitzkysauridae with Megalosauroidea is supported, as future analyses might classify them outside Megalosauroidea.
